steps.message:
`client.py` is shared by both scripts, so this isn't scoped to staging:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (nightly production export for finance)

Setting `verify=False` on the two `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` turns off TLS certificate verification for the production run too — the nightly finance export would accept any certificate, including an attacker's, with no error. Before I touch it:

questions.question: client.py is shared with the production export. How should the self-signed staging cert be handled?

options.label: Scope to staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Make verify configurable (e.g. a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var, or a module-level VERIFY constant) and disable it only in sync_staging.py. Production keeps full certificate verification.

options.label: Trust the staging CA cert
options.description: Point verify at the staging CA/cert bundle path instead of disabling it. Staging connections still validate, production unchanged. Needs the cert file available.

options.label: verify=False on both calls
options.description: Exactly as asked: TLS verification off in client.py for every caller, production nightly export included. Fastest, but production traffic becomes vulnerable to interception.

```python

```

**`scripts/sync_staging.py`** — opts out via `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0`, set before the `client` import just like the existing `REPORTS_BASE_URL` line.

`scripts/export_prod.py` is untouched and keeps full certificate verification, so the nightly finance export is unaffected. Anything else importing `client` also stays verified unless it deliberately opts out.
